title: Portuguese mini-study: four red wines from Casa Ferreirinha, Quinta Nova, Douorum and Rocim
summary: These four Portuguese reds were all purchased from supermarket Pingo Doce and an independent wine shop, while I was teaching
content:
These four Portuguese reds were all purchased from supermarket Pingo Doce and an independent wine shop, while I was teaching in Vila Real.

Casa Ferreirinha Vinha Grande 2023 Douro, Portugal
13% alcohol. 18 months in used French oak. This is beautifully fresh and floral, with a touch of nice green sitting alongside the sweet cherry and raspberry fruit. There’s a touch of olive and cured meat savouriness here as well as some nice grippy tannins providing a foil to the fruit. Massive drinkability and quite a bit of pleasure, and I really like the freshness that this wine has. This could age well over the short term: it’s tight and unfurled. 92/100 (This is cheap in Portugal, at around €12, and about £17 in the UK)

Quinta Nova de Nossa Senhora do Carmo Unoaked 2024 Douro, Portugal
13.5% alcohol. A blend of Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Tinta Roriz and Tinto Cão. This is vivid and fresh with some floral black cherry fruit as well as hints of olive and pepper, then with freshness and a bit of structure on the palate. There’s some really pretty fruit here, but it’s also quite substantial with a bit of grunt. A lovely, well balanced Douro red with a lot of local character. 93/100 (€16.90 in a grocery shop in Vila Real)

Tons de Duorum Talhão 37 2024 Douro, Portugal
13.5% alcohol. Duorum is a collaboration between José Maria Soares Franco and João Portugal Ramos, and this is a private label for supermarket Pingo Doce, where it is for sale at €6.99 from €13.99. This is bright and focused with a spicy, vivid, slightly peppery/tarry/bacon edge to the sweet berry and cherry fruit. There’s freshness and florality here, with a marked contribution from Touriga Nacional, and then some grip and presence on the finish. No jamminess or over-ripeness here. For the price, this is remarkable value. 91/100 (€6.99 Pingo Doce from €13.99)

Vinhas Velhas do Rocim Alicante Bouschet 2024 Alentejo, Portugal
14% alcohol. I think this is another Pingo Doce private label, from the well respected Rocim in Vidigueira in the Alentejo. It’s got a really fresh, fruity, almost jellyish nose with nice cherry, strawberry and ripe plum fruit. In the mouth this is fruity and open with a really supple character, showing juicy fruit and nice brightness. It’s sweet and jellyish, and reminds me a bit of Lodi Zinfandel. 89/100 (€7.99 Pingo Doce promoted from €19.99)

title: An Austrian wine mini-study with seven interesting bottles
summary: These wines were being poured at the Star Wine List Inspiration Day in Stockholm, November 2026. Mayersistas Pet Nat Zweigelt
content:
These wines were being poured at the Star Wine List Inspiration Day in Stockholm, November 2026.

Mayersistas Pet Nat Zweigelt Rosé 2023 Austria
12% alcohol. This is Zweigelt from the Kamptal. Full pink red in colour, this is juicy and bright with pear, cherry and redcurrant flavours. Very fruity and direct, and pure. 91/100

Loimer Brut Nature Blanc de Blancs Grosse Reserve 2020 Langenlois, Austria
This spends 36 months on lees. Intense and lively with a citrus fruit core. This is precise and complex and has great energy. Really impressive. 93/100

Leth Riesling Ried Schillingsberg 2025 Wagram, Austria
This is bright and focused with nice lemony fruit. Lovely acidity and intensity: a very pure, linear expression of Riesling. 92/100

Müller Grossman Furth Grüner Veltliner 2023 Kremstal, Austria
This is a very fresh, crisp style with some citrus and pear fruit. Bright with good energy, and a dose of white pepper. Stylish, pure. 92/100

Hans & Anita Nittnaus Spektra Rosé 2025 Austria
11.5% alcohol. This Zweigelt from Burgenland. Deeply coloured, this is juicy, vivid and fresh with tangy berry fruits, showing brightness allied to personality. Salty, mineral and delicious. 93/100

Muhr Ried Spitzerberg Obere Roterd 1er 2022 Carnuntum, Austria
Supple and stony, this is a restrained, complex expression of Blaufränkisch with red cherry and raspberry fruit, as well as a nice subtle sour twist on the finish. Mineral, bright and energetic. 96/100

Meinhard Markowitsch Purple X-Treme 2020 Carnuntum, Austria
With a name like this I was expecting a big, bold wine but it’s actually quite tasty, with supple, ripe berry fruits and some sour cherry showing good freshness and energy. 93/100

Kracher Welschriesling Trockenbeerenauslese Nummer 2 Zwischen den Seen 2022 Burgenland, Austria
This is brilliant. Lovely sweet flavours of marmalade and lime with ripe melon and beautiful balance, despite the concentration. Quite beautiful. 96/100

title: Gut Oggau: stunningly original, naturally made wines from Austria’s Burgenland
summary: Website: www.gutoggau.com Eduard Tscheppe and his wife Stephanie Tscheppe-Eselböck farm 20 hectares of vines in Austria’s Burgenland region, and their
content:
Website: www.gutoggau.com

Eduard Tscheppe and his wife Stephanie Tscheppe-Eselböck farm 20 hectares of vines in Austria’s Burgenland region, and their winery name is Gut Oggau. They work with old vines which they farm using biodynamics (they are Demeter certified), and they make the wines quite naturally. They were in London at their importer, Dynamic Vines, to share their wines and their story.

‘We chose our approach, which totally feels good for us, and we feel this is the best we can do to express the potential of our soil and of our vineyards,’ says Eduard. ‘But you might talk to another grower, and they might tell you a totally different story. That’s okay, because in the end, the culture is something personal, the connection with the land and the plants is certainly something which you cannot copy and paste, and you have to find your own approach’

‘We started 20 years ago next year, in 2007,’ he says. ‘We had a chance to buy an old estate in the town of Oggau, which is on the west bank of lake Neusidel, close to the Hungarian border in Burgenland.’

The previous owner had lost track, and for 10 years before they took over she hadn’t made any wine.

‘In 2007, the wine world was on a totally different chapter,’ he says. ‘The term natural wine wasn’t born yet.’ He says there were no role models or people to follow. ‘The inspiration we had was also driven a lot through the place, because when we started working with those old vineyards, back then 30-60 years old, we felt we needed to treat them as sensitively as possible to revitalise them.’

And then when it came time to make the wines of this place, again, they had no reference points, so they made them in a non-interventional no-makeup style, which they have continued with.

‘Wine has never been a drink that you can reproduce or standardise; wine has always been this cultural experience of a place combined with a certain time,’ says Eduard. ‘So what we call the vintage is actually all the information collected from the weather, from the climate, from the cosmos into the grapes, and that will never be the same. And what we call terroir is basically all the information and the energy from the soil, from the mother earth, which is also to a certain extent unique, because the roots are ever growing, and the soil is also changing, but it’s a little bit more constant, because usually the roots are where they are, and the mineral components are what they are.’

Their view is that wine carries this sense of place and time, and that then this creates emotions. ‘We can talk about what the wine tastes like, but ideally we would want you to tell us what it makes you feel like.’

Eduard says that what makes their wines special, to an extent, is that they allow us to connect with everything that drives life on the planet, bundled into grapes and then into the wine. ‘It is the forces of the planet Earth, which nurtures us from underneath, and it’s the forces of the vast cosmos around, which nurtures us with energy from above. There would not be life on our planet without those two poles. And this is what Biodynamics is essentially about: respecting those two poles and fine-tuning.’

In terms of their farming, they now work in a more sensitive way, recognizing that everything is connected. This is ancient wisdom, they say. One of the ways they do this in the vineyard is to move away from monoculture and create biodiversity. ‘We plant a lot of trees every year in the vineyards to create a different microclimate, to connect the roots with the mycorrhizae, and to attract birds and insects. We have a lot of cover crops. We also planned a lot of bushes and herbs. So on purpose, we reduce our crop of the grapes, but what we get from this is more resilience and more quality.’

When they made their first wines, they were excited by how different they all were. This is when they came up with the idea of describing each wine in terms of the personality of a person. They did a personal profile on each wine and then imagined faces according to the profile. So each of the Gut Oggau wines is named after a fictional character, created by Jung von Matt, who’s a German designer, and their faces are depicted on the labels, which are quite distinctive. These fictional characters are integrated into a family tree! Eduard feels that the wines have strong personalities, and this anthropomorphism is a way of expressing this. There are children, their parents, and also grandparents. It’s an interesting concept.

They mix and mingle the red and white grapes in their wines, and they don’t alter their vinification on the basis of whether they are using red or white grapes. They macerate the whites on the skins, and then with the reds they’ve pulled back from doing a traditional full maceration, which they think is too much. ‘Freshness in our wines is mainly minerals, not just acidity,’ says Eduard. ‘Too much tannic structure hides a little bit of this beautiful vibrant energy from the soil.’ So they so most of their wines part on skins and part direct pressed. Their only use of sulfites is just before bottling.

In the cellar they use Austrian oak only, from the north of Austria, and the barrels are made by Stockinger. Here the oaks grow very slowly. ‘We always ask for the wood to be aged for more than five years outside, to wash out all the green tannins.’

At one stage they visited Georgia (in 2015) and thought about importing some qvevri, but only reflection they thought it wasn’t right because the qvevri belonged there, in Georgia, not Austria.

Eduard refers to wine as living. ‘In the precious juice which ferments, we still have a lot of microorganisms sleeping, but also doing the job to evolve the wine in a certain direction. And especially after the fermentation, for this ageing period, life leads oxygen.’ For this reason they don’t like stainless steel, except for holding blends just before bottling.

Their view is that there is no good or bad vintage. The question is: how much effort does it take to achieve balanced grapes? Humid years are physically more exhausting, while dry, hot years are mentally more exhausting. ‘We never expect anything at the beginning of the season,’ he says. ‘We embrace the natural conditions.’

Because of the concerns about compaction from repeated treatments against mildew, they are rethinking their grape varieties, and will only be planting resistant varieties going forwards. ‘We will plant only hybrids in the future,’ says Eduard. ‘We have Vitis vinifera which doesn’t have any tolerance against downy and powdery mildew. For us, we feel the time is right to plant [resistant] varieties.’ There’s a nursery that is selling resistant varieties based on Austrian grape varieties that they are using, with Austrian genetics plus tolerance to mildew. ‘People question whether hybrids have the same quality and express terroir,’ says Eduard, ‘but we still graft hybrids, so the connection to the soil is the same through the rootstocks.’ He adds, ‘it’s a big relief for the system.’

‘We never had the intention to provoke with our wines,’ he says, ‘but our wines have been hugely provocative to the wine world. It’s about what people expect from a wine.

Stephanie adds, ‘for you, what is perfection? For you it is something different than it is for me.’

The wines are separated into generations. The younger generation is vineyards on the flat lands (120 m), and then this goes up to the older generation on this hills, which reach 300 m.

Gutt Oggau Anastasius 2025 Burgenland, Austria
This is from 7 parcels on the flatlands, on gravel and limestone soils. This is supple with red cherries and raspberries, with a distinctive stony character under the vivid redcurrant and raspberry fruit, with a savoury twist. Nice acid line. Lovely. 93/100

Gutt Oggau Theodora 2023 Burgenland, Austria
From gravel soils, this is youthful but has substance. Complex and textural with notes of honey, dried grass, lemon, wet stone and spice. Such presence, with nice tension and a hint of ripe apple. 94/100

Gutt Oggau Timotheus 2023 Burgenland, Austria
Limestone/slate soils. Full yellow/gold in colour. Powerful and textural with a bit of structure but also lovely pear and white peach fruit. Not super aromatic but with great concentration, showing a sense of harmony. This is quite beautiful. 95/100

Gutt Oggau Emmeram 2022 Burgenland, Austria
This is a rarity: a single variety. It’s Gewurztraminer, which is too predominant in a blend. Limestone soils. Slightly cloudy full yellow colour. Wonderful aromatics of grapes, pears and some white peach. Lovely freshness allied to depth with a nice acid line, and some warm spicy notes, dried herbs and chalky freshness. There’s a bit of grip here too. 94/100

Gutt Oggau Cecilia 2023 Burgenland, Austria
Limestone soils. On southeast-facing hils, a co-plantation of white and red varieties. Two-thirds white, one-thirds red, co-fermented. Pink in colour, this has lovely fruity aromatics of lime, cherry and herbs. The palate has good energy and focus with vibrant cherry and cranberry fruit, with subtle fine-grained structure and a hint of sour cherry. Lovely. 95/100

Gutt Oggau Josephine 2021 Burgenland, Austria
This is a parent generation wine, and it’s a blend of vineyards that they took over in 2011. These are south facing and are the warmest vineyards they own, and the main grape here is a teinturier hybrid called Roesler. Vivid but very fresh with nice acidity as well as chalky, stony minerality. Fresh with raspberry and blackcurrant fruit, showing lovely depth but also good freshness. 94/100

Gutt Oggau Joschauri 2021 Burgenland, Austria
From stonier soils at 300 m. This has lovely complexity and energy with nice purity. Floral, expressive red cherries and redcurrants. Quite an elegant style with modest structure and a nice acid line. Good intensity here. 95/100

Gutt Oggau Metchtild 2022 Burgenland, Austria
This is the grandparents’ generation, from the oldest vineyards (70+ years), with a mix of limestone and schist. Whole cluster ferment then pressed with a 200 year old restored beam press. Complex, fresh and tannin with lovely energy. There’s a sense of harmony, with notes of orange peel and ripe pear, as well as some grip. Lovely ripeness with some tannins but no bitterness. Such lovely detail and energy. 96/100

Gutt Oggau Bertholdi 2019 Burgenland, Austria
This is Grüner Veltliner and Blaufränkisch, pressed with the old beam press. This has beautiful tension and energy with good acidity under the cherry and raspberry fruit, with wet stone and a touch of redcurrant. Supple and fine with a lovely flow across the palate. Such focus here, quite beautiful. 96/100

UK agent is Dynamic Vines

title: Tasting five of the best from Torres, Penedès, Spain
summary: At the recent Star Wine List Inspiration Day I tasted through these fine wines from leading Catalunyan producer Torres. They
content:
At the recent Star Wine List Inspiration Day I tasted through these fine wines from leading Catalunyan producer Torres. They make a wide range of wines including some great value for money supermarket-style bottles (Viña Sol, for example), but they also do high-end terroir wines. These were all really good.

Torres Varietat Recuperada No 23 Forcada 2022 Penedès, Spain
This is one of the recovered varieties that Torres worked on, and it’s really good. Fresh but textural with some green apple and pear fruit. Very expressive and nicely balanced. 93/100

Torres Milmanda Chardonnay 2022 Conca de Barberà, Spain
Things have changed with this wine. 2022 was the first year they didn’t do malolactic fermentation, and they have reduced the ageing time, as well as using foudres in addition to small oak. Fresh and linear with pear and white peach fruit and some stony detail. Really textured with good weight and balance. 94/100

Torres Mas de la Rosa Vinyes Velles Porrera 2020 Priorat, Spain
This is from a single old vineyard and the first wine was made by Torres in 2016. Textured and fine with lovely silkiness, some rose petal and a hint of aniseed as well as textured red berry fruits. Real finesse and tension here. 96/100

Torres Mas La Plana 2020 Penedès, Spain
An excellent vintage for this wine, which was first made in 1970. Cabernet Sauvignon is the grape. Supple and grainy with black cherries and blackcurrant fruit, showing nice weight and complexity. This has some silky texture and shows great balance with real drinkability. You can approach this now, but it will age, too. 96/100

Torres Grans Muralles 2020 Conca de Barberà, Spain
A blend of Garnacha, Cariñena, Querol, Monastrell and Garró. Bold, rich and pure with lovely blackcurrant and black cherry fruit. This has nice density with real depth and weight. Despite the evident richness from this vineyard this is beautifully balanced. 95/100

title: The wines of Son Antem Alaró, Mallorca, Spain (updated with new releases)
summary: Website: https://www.sonantemalaro.es/en/ Mallorca isn’t well known as a wine island, but there are some interesting projects here, and a recent
content:
Website: https://www.sonantemalaro.es/en/

Mallorca isn’t well known as a wine island, but there are some interesting projects here, and a recent addition to the fine wine scene here is the Son Antem project, which was started by a wine-importing couple in Sweden, Johan and Marin Lidby. I tried through the range and came away impressed.

Son Antem Alaró has 18 hectares of vines, all hand managed by the Lidby family. These are three sets of notes, with the first set from November 2026, the previous set from April 2026 and the third from a year previously.

Son Antem Aura 2024 Mallorca, Spain
Textural and broad with nice balance to the pear fruit, with a hint of white peach. Fine spicy detail. 93/100

Son Antem Camins Blanco 2025 Mallorca, Spain
This is a wine that’s made from the lots left over after blending the other wines. Hint of honey and nice bready notes, with pear and melon fruit. Good weight and balance. 93/100

Son Antem Alba 2024 Mallorca, Spain
Chardonnay. Lively and focused with nice weight, and notes of pear, cherry and citrus. Textural wine that finishes brisk. 93/100

Son Antem Malva 2025 Mallorca, Spain
This is Malvasia, and this year it didn’t ferment to dryness, stopping at 14.5% alchol with 16 g/l residual sugar. Brisk with nice weight, and the sweetness adds texture, and is well countered with good acidity. There’s a touch of sweetness that works well here. Lively and delicious. 93/100

Son Antem S’Era 2023 Mallorca, Spain
Callet. Very pale red in colour, this is supple, smooth and elegant with strawberry and red cherry fruit, as well as a hint of vanilla. Nice balance. 94/100

Son Antem Sa Tanca 2023 Mallorca, Spain
Manto Negro. Pale in colour with supple, nicely weighted cherry and strawberry fruit. Fine spicy notes add interest and it has lovely texture in the mouth. 94/100

Son Antem Camins Negra 2025 Mallorca, Spain
Syrah, Monastrell and a splash of Manto Negro. Juicy, lively and peppery with balanced red cherry fruit and a touch of spice. Lively and very drinkable. 93/100

Son Antem Vespre 2023 Mallorca, Spain
Syrah and Monastrell. Nice weight here with elegant black cherry fruit and some spicy structure. Real purity with some grip. 94/100

Son Antem Malva 2024 Vino de la Tierra Mallorca, Spain
14% alcohol. This white is powerful, rich and intense with a lively acid line lying under the rich pear and peach fruit. The limestone gives the bracing acidity that provides a nice foil for the bold, slightly pithy fruit. Such nice intensity to this distinctive white wine, with a lively acid character driving things. 93/100

Son Antem Aura 2024 Vino de la Tierra Mallorca, Spain
13% alcohol. This white is made from the Giró Rus variety. Bold, rich and textural with some honey, nut and spice characters as well as some pear and peach. There’s innate richness, but it stays fresh and crystalline, with a touch of aniseed and some grainy detail. 92/100

Camins de Son Antem Callet 2024 Vino de la Tierra Mallorca, Spain
12.5% alcohol. This is a lighter-coloured red wine with beautiful aromatics of sweet strawberries and some glace cherry. In the mouth it is very textural with white pepper, cherry, strawberry and fine spicy notes. Lovely fine-grained texture here. Sleek and sweetly fruited with finesse. 94/100

Son Antem S’Era 2024 Vino de la Tierra Mallorca, Spain
12.5% alcohol. Relatively pale in colour, this is is juicy, fine and delicate. There’s a rich mid-palate core of sweet cherry and plum fruit with some damson bitterness, and also some dried herb character. The variety here is Callet, and it seems brilliantly adapted to this warm climate, with some rose, cherry, aniseed and mediterranean herb notes. It’s a little compressed on the finish, with some tannin and acid providing structure, but overall this is really compelling. 94/100

Camins de Son Antem Negre 2024 Vino de la Tierra Mallorca, Spain
14% alcohol. Manto Negro, Monastrell and Syrah. This is sleek, ripe and textured with appealing black cherry and berry fruits. There’s an innate richness and ripeness, but it’s hemmed in by a bit of grainy structure and just enough acidity. And the fruit character stays deliciously floral and fresh. 93/100

Older notes:

Son Antem Camins de Mallorca Giro Blanco 2023 Mallorca, Spain
12.5% alcohol. This is concentrated and grainy and salty with sweet, textured, ripe pear and citrus fruit (a touch of mandarin and lemon). This has such a lovely mineral flow on the palate with real finesse. Very expressive: ripe but well defined. 94/100

Son Antem Malva 2023 Mallorca
14% alcohol. This is really rich and expansive with sweet pear and table grape fruitiness, as well as some spicy highlights and a touch of saltiness. Rich, exuberant and really fruity, this has lots of personality, and good acidity balancing the sweet fruit. 91/100

Son Antem Camins de Mallorca Rouge 2022 Mallorca, Spain
12.5% alcohol. Lovely aromatics here with sleek cherries, raspberries and some aniseed, as well as a hint of pepper. The palate has a sweet fruit core with nice spicy detail. Pure and refined with warm Mediterranean herb notes but always so balanced with real finesse. Grainy and delicious. 93/100

Son Antem Alaró S’Era 2023 IGP Mallorca, Spain
12% alcohol. This is varietal Callet. Quite a pale cherry red colour, in the in-between land, not quite rosé, not quite red wine. Very fine and supple with sweet red cherry fruit and a silky elegance, and just a hint of structure. Has lovely texture and warmth with rounded sweet cherry fruit. 94/100

Son Antem Vespre 2022 Mallorca, Spain
12.5% alcohol. This is supple, expressive and elegant with real elegance, and a sweet, textured mid-palate with stony cherries and plums, and then notes of herbs, pepper and fine spices framing the fruit on the finish. This is very fine: restrained, sappy and showing warm-climate elegance. 94/100

Son Antem Sa Tanca 2022 Mallorca, Spain
13% alcohol. This is Manto Negro, from iron-rich stony soils. Beautiful aromatics: sweet cherry and raspberry fruit with some nice spicy detail and a beautiful flow across the palate. Ripe but really elegance with great purity. 95/100

title: Clau de Nell, the Anjou (Loire) estate from Christian Jacques and Anne-Claude Leflaive
summary: It was back in 2008 that Christian Jacques and Anne Claude Leflaive purchased the struggling Clau de Nell domaine, initially
content:
It was back in 2008 that Christian Jacques and Anne Claude Leflaive purchased the struggling Clau de Nell domaine, initially with a view to running it with the existing owner who was experiencing financial difficulties. Soon, though, they realized they’d have to run it themselves if it was going to work.

Jacques and Leflaive already knew Clau de Nell because it was part of a portfolio of 13 biodynamic domaines that they were selling. But the domaine was in such trouble that it hadn’t made wine for three years.

In 2009 Jacques was joined by winemaker Sylvain Potin, and they set about restoring the vineyards. It’s a single, rather isolated plot of 12 hectares on a gentle slope, and as well as the Cabernet Franc and Grolleau vines, they’ve planted some Chenin Blanc. There’s also a bit of Cabernet Sauvignon, too. ‘Grolleau is very important for us,’ says Sylvain. ‘It’s our native grape variety and these are 90-100 year old vines.’

It’s quite significant that the vines are just in one block, with no other vines nearby. The neighbouring forests and farmland add biodiversity.

The property is named after the previous owners, who hailed from Burgundy, called Claude and Nelly Pichard. Clau de Nell has now been farmed biodynamically since 2000.

Anne-Claude passed in 2015, but Christian has carried on with Clau de Nell, and his late wife’s name is still on the bottles. His three daughters, Marine, Charlotte and Claire, are actively involved with the estate now. They are based in Burgundy, but Sylvain is the local person and lives in the Loire.

I tasted these wines with Sylvain Potin at the headquarters of his UK importer, Corney & Barrow. The pictures of the vineyards are from a visit in May 2017.

Clau de Nell Blanc de Noir 2022 Vin de France
This is a cuvée that has been made since 2020, from Cabernet Franc. It’s the latest ripening block, and they just keep the heart of the pressing to make a white wine. It’ spends 18 months in a neutral barrel. Textural with pear, peach and cherry, as well as some almond detail. Quite rich. 92/100

Clau de Nell Blanc de Noir 2023 Vin de France
Linear and focused with nice citrus and pear fruit. Lovely tension and balance with a fruity core. 93/100

Clau de Nell Chenin Blanc 2023 Anjou, Loire, France
Vines planted in 2012 on limestone/clay soils, south-facing plot. The vines were grafted with the greffe anglaise, and the material is mass selection. This has depth but also some delicacy with pear, citrus and white peach, and a nice reductive twist. There’s richness as well as crystalline focus. Nice tension. 95/100

Clau de Nell Grolleau 2020 IGP Val de Loire, France
Floral and bright with lovely cherry fruit and some raspberry notes too. Floral with a touch of wild strawberry and some peppery hints to the textured fruit. Fine and elegant. 94/100

Clau de Nell Cabernet Franc 2020 Loire, France (magnum)
Fresh, fine, textured and linear with a chalky undercurrent to the sweet raspberry and cherry fruit. Supple and elegant with a nice acid line. 96/100

Clau de Nell Cabernet Franc 2022 Loire, France
Very fine and expressive with a chalky edge to the red cherry and raspberry fruit, with a sour cherry twist. Lovely finesse, and really nice fine-grained tannins. 95/100

Clau de Nell Cuvée Violette 2019 Anjou, Loire, France (magnum)
This is the only blend at the estate, and it brings together Cabernets Franc and Sauvignon. Both are old vine. Concentrated and dense showing blackcurrant and black cherry fruit with some meaty density. Hints of pepper and olives. Powerful, quite tannic, but fine with nice depth. 94/100

Clau de Nell Cuvée Violette 2020 Loire, France
Meaty and firm with lovely bright berry fruits. Notes of blackcurrant and sour cherry with nice spicy detail and a chalky edge to the fruit. Vivid, powerful and focused, showing a savoury twist. 94/100

UK agent: Corney & Barrow

title: Tasting some Ports from Quinta do Infantado, an important Douro producer
summary: Website: https://quintadoinfantado.com/en/ Infantado is a family-owned Quinta dating back to 1816. They were famous for being the first quinta to
content:
Website: https://quintadoinfantado.com/en/

Infantado is a family-owned Quinta dating back to 1816. They were famous for being the first quinta to bottle Port wines in the Douro region in 1979, rather than sending the wine to Vila Nova de Gaia. Until 1986 when the laws changed, Port producers weren’t allowed to export wine that didn’t go through Gaia, which created a financial hurdle that ended up keeping small players out of the game. So for a number of years, Infantado made Ports and sold them domestically, before they were allowed to export. Infantado were also among the first in the region to farm organically, starting back in 1990.

Infantado are based in a privileged part of the valley, in Covas de Douro in the Cima Corgo, not far from Pinhão. They have 46 hectares of vineyards. João Roseira heads things (pictured top) up assisted by his cousin, Alváro Roseira (pictured above, with João), who is in charge of winemaking. Recently they have started a negociant arm, with the wines bottled Infantado as opposed to Quinta do Infantado.

The Ports are aged in the old cellar, which is quite beautiful, and even has some resident bats. Usually about 60% of the Infantado production is Port. These Ports were on show at the tasting of their new UK importers, Graft, who for now just take the Ports and not the also-excellent table wines.

Quinta do Infantado White Port NV Douro, Portugal
19.5% alcohol. This is a blend of Gouveio, Rabigato, Viosinho and Moscatel Galego, sourced from grade ‘A’ vineyards (Pousado, Serra de Cotas and Vale de Moinhos, totally 3.5 hectares in all. Partially destemmed, fermented in lagar and tank with 6 months maceration after  fermentation is stopped with 77% alcohol brandy and then aged in an 8000 litre old wooden tank and some smaller casks. Orange/gold in colour this is powerful and intense with notes of orange peel, mint and spice. Lively with amazing complexity and some tannin. 94/100

Quinta do Infantado Ruby Port NV Douro, Portugal
19.5% alcohol. Sourced from grade ‘A’ vineyards (Serra Douro, Lapa, Castelos, 10 hectares in all). Whole bunches, foot trodden in lagar, fortified with 77% brandy and aged 24-30 months in old wooden tanks. João calls this his ‘Beaujolais Villages’ Port. Ripe, rich and fruit driven with lovely weight, showing some pepper spice, sweet cherries and plums and lovely refinement. Great fruit intensity. 93/100

Quinta do Infantado Late Bottled Vintage Port 2021 Douro, Portugal
The driest Port they have ever made with just 50 g/l sugar. This has lovely energy with some sweetness but also good structure. Dried herbs and spice, as well as some pepper. Nice definition here. 94/100

Quinta do Infantado Vintage Port 2015 Douro, Portugal

title: Famille Morin, an impressive Beaujolais domaine based in Chiroubles
summary: Website: https://www.domainefamillemorin.fr/nos-vins-du-beaujolais/ Chiroubles-based Famille Morin is making some excellent Beaujolais wines. I tasted with Théo Morin at an event run
content:
Website: https://www.domainefamillemorin.fr/nos-vins-du-beaujolais/

Chiroubles-based Famille Morin is making some excellent Beaujolais wines. I tasted with Théo Morin at an event run by their UK importer Woodwinters.

I was really impressed by these wines from Famille Morin, who are based in one of the most interesting Crus in Beaujolais, Chiroubles. This is a cru with higher altitude and almost all granitic soils (you might be surprised to learn that there’s quite a bit of variation in Beaujolais and it’s not all granite soils), and it’s hilly.

Théo Morin, who runs the domaine with his parents, says that it’s complicated working the slopes, which can be 25-40%, and this means lots of manual work, especially because they farm organically. They also do some agroforestry. Most of the reds are made with carbonic maceration of around 10 days, and then they press and finish off the ferments in the juice phase at low temperatures.

Famille Morin Beaujolais Villages Blanc 2025 France
Older oak. Bright and direct with lovely citrus drive. This is pure, textural and fine with fine-grained chalky minerality. 93/100

Famille Morin Beaujolais Villages Rouge 2024 France
Fresh and linear, this is a bright expression of Gamay showing lovely redcurrant and red cherry fruit. Such purity and finesse, showing nice directness. 93/100

Famille Morin Chiroubles 2024 Beaujolais, France
A blend of different plots, carbonic maceration. Lovely tension here: this is floral and pretty with a stony minerality. Really expressive with strawberries and raspberries. Stylish. 94/100

Famille Morin Chiroubles Vielles Vignes 2023 Beaujolais, France
98 year old vines. 20-25 day maceration, then 18 months in foudre. Structured, bright and vivid. Juicy and lively with nice tension and some structure. Fine and expressive. 94/100

Famille Morin Morgon Terrain Rouge 2024 Beaujolais, France
This is from red schist soils. Lovely redcurrant and raspberry fruit. Bright and expressive with lovely weight and purity. Very fine grained with nice tension. 94/100

Famille Morin Gamaret 2024 France
This is from Chiroubles, and it’s a crossing between Reichensteiner and Gamay made in Switzerland in 1970. Intense, vivid and powerful with freshness to the raspberry and black cherry fruit. Expressive with a saline twist. 93/100

title: Domaine du Pélican: the Jura venture of Guillaume d’Angerville
summary: Guillaume d’Angerville (pictured above) was in town to show the wines of his Jura winery, Domaine du Pélican. He began
content:
Guillaume d’Angerville (pictured above) was in town to show the wines of his Jura winery, Domaine du Pélican. He began this project in 2012, but the story goes back to 2007 when he started looking for vineyards in the Jura. At the time it wasn’t as fashionable as it is now, but he wanted to be there.

He came back to his family estate. Domaine Marquis d’Angerville, in 2003 after the death of his father, Jacques. This Volnay-based estate had been in the family for 200 years. He inherited it, but after he’d been humbled in a blind tasting where he’d decided that an Arbois was in fact a Puligny-Montrachet, he set his eyes on the Jura. ‘It was close enough to Burgundy that I could sign my name on the label without lying,’ he says.

‘Initially I bought five hectares from a guy who had replanted the entire estate,’ he told me. ‘So the vineyard was in a good shape. The terroir was interesting.’ And later in in 2007 he bought another 5 hectares in Arbois, in a famous lieu dit called Grand Coroulet. ‘This needed a lot of work,’ says Guillaume, ‘and I ended up uprooting the whole lot.’ But he says that for a Burgundy guy it was a bit of a dream finding a vineyard of this size all in one block.

Five years later, he got another 5 hectares from Jacques Puffeney, whose winery was just down the road from Pélican.

‘Jura was nowhere then. The resurrection of Jura and alpine wines was around this time. I was lucky.’ Prior to the current fame of this region, most of the wines were drunk locally. ‘80% of the Jura wines were consumed in Jura,’ says Guillaume. ‘I was the first to come in from another region.’ So now he has 15 hectares, with a 70:30 white:red split.

Domaine du Pélican Brut S Zero Brut Nature 2020 Vin de France
Guillaume wanted to make a sparkling wine in Jura just with Savagnin, so this is why it isn’t Crémant de Jura, and why he can’t put Savagnin on the label. It’s the only sparkling 100% Savagnin from the region. Bright and fruity with mandarin, pear and lime, and a touch of spice on the finish. 92/100

Domaine du Pélican Savagnin Ouillé 2023 Arbois, Jura, France
Textural and refined with sweet cherry and pear, as well as some citrus. Pure and mineral laced with good balance and weight, finishing with a touch of aniseed. 94/100

Domaine du Pélican Savagnin Ouillé 2022 Arbois, Jura, France
Crystalline and taut with lovely acidity. Mineral and bright with cherry, pear, apple and spice. Rich but with tension, and quite lovely. 94/100

Domaine du Pélican Savagnin Ouillé Grand Coroulet 2022 Arbois, Jura, France
Subtle toast, honey and meal on the nose as well as lemon and mandarin. Fine, textural palate is pure and refined. Polished showing elegance and focus, with a saline finish. 94/100

Domaine du Pélican Chardonnay 2023 Arbois, Jura, France
Such a pretty wine: delicately toasty with sweet pear and peach fruit. Fine toast and marzipan notes. Very expressive. 94/100

Domaine du Pélican Chardonnay en Barbi 2023 Arbois, Jura, France
So textural, with pear and peach as well as some citrus and a touch of aniseed. Nice weight on the palate which shows some honeyed richness, and then it’s pure and expressive on the finish. Very refined. 95/100

Domaine du Pélican Savagnin Macération Pelliculaire 2022 Arbois, Jura, France
Complex and aromatic with a touch of structure. Nice depth with appealing citrus and apple. Powerful yet elegant, with some grip. 95/100

Domaine du Pélican Trois Cépages 2023 Arbois, Jura, France
This wine started because in the debut year there were so few red grapes Guillaume didn’t want to vinify them separately, so it’s a blend of around 60% Pinot Noir with Trousseau and Ploussard. It works very well: the Pinot is dominant, but the Trousseau gives spice and the Poulsard gives a smooth finish. Very fine with redcurrant, red cherry and some sour cherry. Nice acidity. Redcurrant and cherry fruit with nice detail and good acidity. 95/100

Domaine du Pélican Trois Cépages 2022 Arbois, Jura, France
Fresh, lively and textured with red cherry and redcurrant, as well as wild strawberry and spice, with some dried herbs too. Lots of personality here. Lively and complex, but elegant with simplicity, but also precision and beauty. 94/100

Domaine du Pélican Trousseau Béranger 2023 Arbois, Jura, France
This is very pale in colour. Lovely cherry and citrus with some redcurrant, red cherries and plums. So fresh and firm, tapering, elegant and pure. 96/100

Domaine du Pélican Savagnin Sous Voile 2020 Arbois, Jura, France
Three years under flor. Highly aromatic: tangy with a flor character, but it’s refined and quite delicate. Notes of mint, pear and lime as well as tangy apple fruit. Such a detailed, tart wine. Elegant and long. 96/100

Domaine du Pélican Savagnin Sous Voile 2019 Arbois, Jura, France
This spends 3 years under the flor, while the Vin Jaune spends 6 years. Fresh and tangy with real interest. Salty and intense with real complexity and focus, showing green apple and cherry as well as lemony fruit. Delicate and pure. 95/100

Domaine du Pélican Vin Jaune 2016 Arbois, Jura, France
Six years under flor. Juicy, tangy and vivid. Powerful with bice density. Complex and layered, this is oily, spicy and vivid with real power and precision. Tightwound and profound. 97/100

title: Bordeaux 2024 vintage in bottle, assessing 100 of the top wines from this tricky vintage
summary: Once again, a chance to look through the latest Bordeaux vintage courtesy of the Union des Grands Crus at their
content:
Once again, a chance to look through the latest Bordeaux vintage courtesy of the Union des Grands Crus at their annual London tasting. It was the turn of 2024.

I avoid the primeurs each year because I don’t see too much value in tasting barrel samples and then writing extensive notes. You aren’t seeing the final wine, you will probably be tasting a blend that has been prepared specially for the occasion and aged in fancy barrels, and unless you are a winemaker you will have very limited experience of seeing a baby wine progress to become a bottled wine.

Still, lots of the trade and press spend quite a bit of time in Bordeaux each year joining this circus and writing extensively about these barrel samples as if they were the real, finished wine. The scores given at this early stage creates an anchoring effect that may be misleading, and the system also favours the established top producers. Rather than take part in the UGC tasting, a bunch of fancy producers insist you come to them. Everything is tasted sighted. It makes it hard for a ‘lesser’ producer doing really good work to get recognized.

The only time I’ll taste and write about the new vintage is very occasionally when producers bring samples to the UK, but then I hope I’m giving a strong caution that these are just samples, not finished wines. (An example of this is here: https://wineanorak.com/2026/06/03/a-quick-appraisal-of-the-2025-vintage-in-bordeaux/)

So the UGC tasting is normally my first look at the wines from a new vintage. It’s still a challenge looking at so many wines in close proximity, but it’s a great chance to take a deep dive into the latest releases. My impression of the 2024 vintage is that there are some fine wines, but it isn’t a great one. The reds are, on the whole, classically proportioned, perhaps on the lighter side, and where producers have recognized the vintage and extracted accordingly (without trying to make the wines bigger) the results should provide some lovely drinking in the medium term.

It was a very difficult vintage, one of the hardest in recent years, but many of these wines are delicious. At the right price they are worth buying, but they won’t go up in price so there’s no hurry to tuck in.

For Bordeaux, this was definitely the wrong vintage at the wrong time, but many châteaux have risen above the challenges and made some smart wines. And the whites are really good.
